free_tier.stated: Free and fully open source. Stable URLs derived from your SSH key. No accounts.

egress.terms: no quota published; the offer is 'Free and fully open source' with no account and no stated cap; ingress: http-only

chaining: HTTP ingress only; composes with a web service and nothing that needs UDP
binding_note: Nothing in the vocabulary binds because the transport cannot carry a UDP datagram at all; the limit is protocol, not quantity.

identity_cost.detail: an SSH key pair and nothing else: 'Stable URLs derived from your SSH key. No accounts.'

reliability_note: one operator (xmit dev team); the tunnel lives only while the ssh session lives
confidence_note: Raise by attempting a UDP forward with ssh -R and recording the server's refusal; not attempted because the service is documented as an HTTP terminator.

evidence.proved: 'Yet another solution to expose any HTTP server to the Internet through a tunnel', 'Free & fully open source. Stable URLs derived from your SSH key. No accounts.'

notes: Worth reading because it is the rare no-account service with a stable address, which is the property WireGuard needs. The protocol excludes it.

extras.wg_detail: the service terminates TLS and speaks HTTP: 'expose any HTTP server to the Internet through a tunnel' and returns https URLs, so there is no UDP path
extras.volume_stated: no quota published; the offer is 'Free and fully open source' with no account and no stated cap
